headline: intg-prod-a1: cause not established — audit log outstanding, convergence blocked. setroubleshootd at 99.7% CPU since 2026-03-02 is driving batch latency and console slowness; the SELinux AVC denial storm behind it has not been directly observed.
known: Process snapshot at 2026-03-17T19:00:00+00:00 shows pid 3501048 (setroubleshootd, user audit-analysis) at 99.7% CPU with 79h 58m cumulative CPU time, started 2026-03-02T06:00:00+00:00 (E-1).
SELinux is confirmed in enforcing mode; denials are real and being logged (E-2).
Integration service JVM (pid 3489339) is at 5.6% CPU with 24.8 GiB resident set at snapshot time.

13 memory exhaustion problems (P-4100 through P-4112) opened in the 03:00–04:00 UTC window and auto-closed approximately 2.5 hours later on each occasion; none were acknowledged, assigned, or actioned.
Memory series shows a rising sawtooth pattern beginning 2026-03-02T00:00:00+00:00, coinciding with onset of problems.
CHG-88104 (endpoint-compliance-agent 7.4.2-27) is the only change record in the pre-onset window, installed 2026-02-22.
The audit-analysis-server package has been installed for 3 years; the 2026-03-02T06:00:00+00:00 event is an activation, not an installation.
JVM steady-state resident set has been 23.1 GiB for at least 6 months, leaving approximately 8.9 GiB free at baseline on a 32 GiB host.
The audit log request was made to platform_team 149 minutes ago and remains outstanding.
The change registry carries a confirmed caveat: self_updating_agents_not_reflected=true — agents that self-update produce no package records.
No pipeline deployments are recorded for intg-prod-a1; application-layer changes delivered outside the pipeline are invisible to the change registry.
intg-nonprod-a1 has build_parity=false with a different patch level and different installed agents.
suspected: SUPPORTED — setroubleshootd is consuming ~100% CPU in response to a high-volume stream of SELinux AVC denials that began 2026-03-02, and this CPU saturation is the proximate cause of batch transfer latency and console slowness on intg-prod-a1. Falsifying test: inspect /var/log/audit/audit.log for AVC denial counts per hour from 2026-03-02 onward; if denial volume is low or absent, setroubleshootd CPU consumption has a different cause not yet identified. Caveat: no direct observation of AVC denial volume or rate exists; the audit log is outstanding, so the link between setroubleshootd CPU and a denial storm is currently inferential.

PLAUSIBLE — endpoint-compliance-agent 7.4.2-27 (CHG-88104), or a self-updated version of it, triggered novel SELinux AVC denials that activated setroubleshootd on 2026-03-02. Falsifying test: inspect /var/log/audit/audit.log for AVC denials from 2026-02-22 through 2026-03-02; if no denials are attributable to the endpoint-compliance-agent source domain, this hypothesis is falsified. Also confirm whether the agent was active and consuming memory between 2026-02-22 and 2026-03-01; flat memory during that period weakens the correlation. Caveats: the 8-day gap between installation and onset weakens temporal proximity; the registry caveat self_updating_agents_not_reflected=true means the version running at onset may differ from 7.4.2-27 with no registry evidence; no AVC denial log yet collected to confirm the agent is the source domain.

PLAUSIBLE — the integration service JVM has a memory leak contributing to the rising sawtooth memory pattern, with the resident set growing during each batch cycle and partially recovering, compounding memory exhaustion alongside setroubleshootd. Falsifying test: collect a JVM heap dump from pid 3489339; if heap occupancy is stable and within historical norms, the JVM is not contributing to the memory growth pattern; swap metrics would also clarify whether the JVM is being paged out during exhaustion events. Caveats: JVM CPU is only 5.6%, inconsistent with a runaway workload; the sharp sawtooth drop is more consistent with a process restart or GC event than a leak; the current 24.8 GiB reading is elevated above the 23.1 GiB baseline but not dramatically so. Precedent cited: INC-2411 described memory exhaustion on an integration-class host with a JVM workload; divergence from that precedent — INC-2411 had a recorded heap configuration change, which is absent here.

SUPPORTED — 13 unacknowledged auto-closing problems over 15 days masked a progressive degradation that has now manifested as user-visible latency. Falsifying test: compare batch transfer completion times and console response times on days when problems were open versus closed; if performance is identical in both states, the auto-closing events are not causing user-visible impact. Caveat: auto-close could reflect genuine recovery if the batch workload completes and memory is released; the pattern alone does not confirm suppression of a worsening condition. Precedent cited: INC-2419 showed the same signature and auto-close behaviour, ran 10 days unacknowledged before action; divergence — INC-2419 was resolved by restart without establishing cause, and that outcome must not be repeated here.
outstanding: Audit denial log for the affected window (source domain and denied action per denial), covering 2026-02-22 through present — requested from platform_team 149 minutes ago, still not received. This is the deciding evidence; convergence is blocked until it is in hand.

setroubleshootd log (/var/log/setroubleshoot/setroubleshoot.log) from 2026-03-02T06:00:00+00:00 onward — requested from security_engineering, still outstanding. Required to identify which SELinux denials are being analysed and confirm denial volume consistent with 99.7% CPU.

Currently running version of endpoint-compliance-agent on intg-prod-a1 — requested from security_engineering, still outstanding. Required to determine whether the agent has self-updated beyond 7.4.2-27 since 2026-02-22.

JVM heap dump and thread dump from pid 3489339 — requested from platform_engineering, still outstanding. Required to characterise whether memory growth is attributable to a workload change or internal leak.

Swap utilisation metric series for intg-prod-a1 at 1h resolution from 2026-03-02 to present — requested from platform_engineering, still outstanding. Required to determine whether the JVM or other processes are being paged out during exhaustion events.
asks: platform_team: the audit log request is 149 minutes old and is the single item blocking convergence — escalate now and deliver /var/log/audit/audit.log from intg-prod-a1 covering 2026-02-22 through present; we need AVC denial counts per hour and source domains extracted.

security_engineering: retrieve /var/log/setroubleshoot/setroubleshoot.log from intg-prod-a1 from 2026-03-02T06:00:00+00:00 onward, and separately confirm the currently running version of endpoint-compliance-agent via agent CLI or /var/lib/endpoint-compliance-agent/version — both are read-only, no production state change.

platform_engineering: run jcmd 3489339 GC.heap_info and jstack 3489339 on intg-prod-a1 to capture JVM heap and thread state, and pull swap.used at 1h resolution for intg-prod-a1 from 2026-03-02 to present from the observability platform — all read-only operations.

incident_commander to all: do not restart setroubleshootd or the integration service JVM until the audit log and setroubleshootd log have been collected and the source of AVC denials identified; a restart would suppress the symptom without establishing the cause and would destroy in-memory state needed for diagnosis. Authorisation is required before any such action is taken.

incident_commander to business stakeholders: notify that the investigation is active, that batch latency is caused by host resource exhaustion under investigation, that no transfers have failed, and provide a next update time.
